messages.content: Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle

reasoning: The user wants an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle. I want to make this a crafted, detailed illustration rather than a bare diagram — give it an ambient, layered background, motion, micro-interactions, hover effects, and a bit of typographic personality, all embedded as a single SVG file (self-contained, with its own CSS/SMIL animations). Let me design a scene: a pelican riding a bicycle, side view, pedaling along a seaside road (pelicans = coastal). Background: sky gradient, sun, layered clouds, distant sea, dunes, boardwalk planks, palm/frond silhouettes, speed lines, seagulls. The bicycle wheels spin, the pedals/crank rotate, the pelican's legs pedal, its beak-pouch wobbles slightly, a scarf flutters, small "wobble" animation of the whole rig, sun glow pulse, clouds drifting, seagulls flying. Palette: a coastal scene wants warm sun over teal sea and sand. Let me do: sky gradient teal-to-warm-cream, sea deep teal, sand ochre, sun amber, pelican body warm bone/ivory, wings slate blue-gray with a teal cast, beak and pouch coral/orange, bike cherry-red frame with mint accents, tire charcoal, spokes light. Good contrast. Typography: I want an expressive display face paired with a readable body face. For the coastal, retro-poster vibe I'll pick display = 'Fraunces' (a wonky soft serif with optical sizing and a SOFT/WONK axis) and body = 'Karla' — the wonky serif fits a pelican perfectly and the geometric grotesque keeps captions legible. I'll include a @import inside the SVG's style (works if opened directly in a browser, since SVG loaded as a document can fetch web fonts); with a fallback stack, so if the fonts don't load it still looks fine. Structure: Single SVG, viewBox e.g. 0 0 1200 750. Include: - defs: gradients (sky, sea, sand, sun glow, frame metal, pouch, feather), filters (soft blur for glow, subtle shadow), patterns (road texture/dashes maybe), clip paths (sea horizon), markers. - Ambient background layers with slow drift animations. - Parallax hills/dunes scrolling to suggest motion. - The bicycle: two wheels with spokes + tires + rims, rotating; frame (diamond frame), handlebar, seat, crank + pedals, chain, chainring, fender, rear rack with a fish bucket, headlight, bell. - Pelican: body ellipse, wing (folded, on handlebar), long neck S-curve, big head, huge beak with throat pouch, eye with blink, crest feathers, legs pedaling (animated), feet on pedals, a scarf flapping. - Motion: speed lines, dust motes, wheel rotation, crank rotation, pedal legs, sway, scarf wave, pouch wobble, sun rays rotating, gulls flapping, cloud drift, road dashes translating. - Micro-interactions: hover on the pelican makes it do something (scale, "honk" speech bubble?), hover on wheels speeds up spin, hover on the bell rings (bell wiggles + sound waves appear), CSS :hover in SVG works when rendered inline or as standalone document. Also a "toggle wind" checkbox? In pure SVG you can use CSS :hover and animations. Let me keep hover interactions and maybe a clickable group toggling classes with a small inline script — SVG supports ``` Chips: give ids `chip-dusk`, `chip-notes`, `chip-honk`. Use a root group `#stage` with classes instead. I'll wrap all content in `` and toggle classes on it. CSS selectors like `#stage.dusk .stars {opacity:1}`. Good, works both inline and standalone. Honk: on click, add class 'honk' to #stage for 900ms → the bubble shows and the beak opens. Also hovering the rig shows the bubble. Notes toggle: `#stage.no-notes .callouts {opacity:0; pointer-events:none}` with a transition. Also chips need `cursor:pointer` and hover styles; make text non-selectable.
